newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Nov 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Nov 26.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum leaders on Monday agreed to reduce tariffs on a wide range of products starting January 1 and to complete the process by 2020. (THE PHILIPPINE STAR)

- Activists opposed to the APEC summit clashed on Monday with pro-APEC groups outside Subic freeport where 18 Pacific rim leaders were meeting. Police said at least 10 people were injured. (THE MANILA CHRONICLE)

- Makati Congressman Joker Arroyo said on Monday he may challenge before the Supreme Court the approval by the House of Representatives of the Comprehensive Tax Reform Programme. (THE MANILA CHRONICLE)

- Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong of Singapore said his country would push for a broader dialogue on the APEC agenda to include macroeconomic, political and security issues when the group meets next year in Vancouver, Canada, for the fifth summit. (THE MANILA TIMES)

- The war between supporters and opponents of APEC is spilling on to the internet. From the Filipino APEC observers point of view, it seems that the anti-APEC groups are winning. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
- Chinese President Jiang Zemin begins a three-day state visit to the Philippines on Tuesday. (MALAYA)

- Philippine President Ramos will risk sounding like a broken record by repeating to Chinese President Jiang Zemin that the Chinese structures in Panganiban Reef should be removed immediately to improve the atmosphere in the Spratlys Islands, foreign policy experts said. (TODAY)

- Philippine Vice President Joseph Estrada, who was miffed on Saturday when an American security man prevented him from getting too close to Bill Clinton, was embarassed again on Monday when he went to see off Clinton but had difficulties approaching his aircraft. (TODAY)

- Starting January, the Board of Investments will be tightening registration rules for exports producers and will require the submission of documents proving they export 70 percent of their total production. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
- The Petroleum Authority of Thailand will put up some 250 gas stations in the country starting March next year to launch its challenge against the three local oil firms. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
